claims.hypothesis: Substructure is ubiquitous in compact protoplanetary discs when observed on spatial scales of ~4 au.
claims.experiment: Observed the compact wide-binary discs Sz 65 and Sz 66 with long-baseline ALMA Band 6 continuum imaging (0''.026 × 0''.018 beam, ~4.0 × 2.8 au) and non-parametric visibility modelling with frank.
claims.result: Detected a shallow gap at ~20 au and an outer ring at 24 au (8% contrast) in Sz 65, whereas Sz 66 (R90 = 16 au) shows a smooth radial profile with no resolved annular substructure.
claims.finding: Substructures can exist in compact discs (as in Sz 65), supporting the presence of structure at high resolution, though Sz 66 remains smooth without clearly identifiable annular substructures.

evidence.quote: Using long-baseline ALMA observations of two class II discs, we test the claim that substructure is ubiquituous in compact discs on spatial scales of ~ 4 au.

The structure we detect in Sz 65 supports the claim that substructure is ubiquituous at sufficiently high angular resolution. Sz 66, however, remains compact and lacks clearly identifiable substructures even at high resolution.

claims.hypothesis: Compact discs in star-forming surveys are simply radially scaled-down versions of bright, extended, multi-ringed DSHARP discs.
claims.experiment: Compared the deprojected 1.3 mm brightness temperature profiles and morphology of Sz 65 and Sz 66 against the full DSHARP sample, the compact DSHARP subset, and CX Tau.
claims.result: Sz 65 and Sz 66 lack deep multiple gaps and outer rings, showing only a low-contrast outer feature in Sz 65 and a sharp outer edge of mm dust, matching the compact DSHARP discs and CX Tau.
claims.finding: Compact discs are not simply size-scaled versions of extended structured discs; instead they likely lack efficient dust traps in the outer disc.

evidence.quote: Our observations of two compact discs and the comparison with the most compact members of the DSHARP sample do not support the interpretation that compact discs in large surveys are simply scaled-down versions of the extended highly structured cases
The observations do not support the hypothesis that these two discs are simply radially smaller size-scaled versions of the bright radially extended DSHARP discs that show multiple substructures.

claims.hypothesis: The compact radial extents of Sz 65 and Sz 66 are primarily caused by radial dust drift or by tidal truncation from their wide-binary interaction.
claims.experiment: Measured R90 sizes of dust and 12CO gas to compute R_gas/R_dust ratios, searched for kinematic perturbations with eddy, and ran Monte Carlo models of binary tidal truncation radii R_t.
claims.result: Sz 65 has R_gas/R_dust = 5.3 ± 0.9 (> 4) and R90_gas = 142 ± 15 au (vs most likely R_t = 276 au); Sz 66 has R_gas/R_dust = 2.9 ± 1.0 and R90_gas = 48 ± 15 au (vs most likely R_t = 195 au, with only 7% of solutions smaller).
claims.finding: Sz 65's high gas-to-dust size ratio indicates significant grain growth and radial drift, whereas tidal truncation is unlikely to be the primary driver of the measured disc sizes in either star unless the binary orbit has very high eccentricity.

evidence.quote: The ratio of R gas / R dust for Sz 65 is 5.3 ± 0.9. This high ratio may indicate significant grain growth and radial drift in the disc (Trapman et al. 2020).
Only 7% of the solutions for Rt are smaller than the derived R 90 for Sz 66.
From this analysis, there is not sufficient evidence that tidal truncation is the primary influence in setting the disc sizes we measure.

why_this_data.value: Long-baseline ALMA observations were combined with four archival datasets in more compact configurations to achieve ~4 au resolution for substructure searches while filling in short uv spacings to recover extended emission.

evidence.quote: The continuum observations achieve a synthesised beam size of 0''.026 × 0''.018, equivalent to about 4.0 × 2.8 au, enabling a search for substructure on these spatial scales and a characterisation of the gas and dust disc sizes with high precision.

We concatenate these archival data to our new observations in order to ensure a more complete coverage of the uv plane. This was necessary in particular to fill in the shorter-baseline spacings lacking from the extended configuration of the new observations.

why_this_method.value: Non-parametric visibility fitting with frank (log-normal method) was used to achieve super-resolution and produce a smoother profile less prone to fitting noisy small-amplitude rings; applymode='calonly' was used on extended configurations to avoid flagging long baselines; a 0''.07 uv taper and 1 km/s spectral averaging were applied to 12CO to boost SNR for a robust detection.

evidence.quote: The log-normal version results in a smoother brightness profile with radius, as the fit is less prone to fitting rings of small amplitude or in noisier baseline ranges.
Averaging of the spectral windows from 122kHz channels to 768kHz (1 km/s) channels was required in order to extract significant emission from the 12 CO (2-1) line.
The log-normal version results in a smoother brightness profile with radius, as the fit is less prone to fitting rings of small amplitude or in noisier baseline ranges.
